summary: ALL SEVEN TARGET ROWS ARE FILLER. AFL is RIGHT on 7 of 7, and the 'STRONG type_source_disagreement' that put them in this wave is a phantom: on SIX of the seven (90, 123, 124, 131, 134, 156) animefillerguide does not make the positive claim at all — its own row carrying that episode's TITLE reads '*Filler | N/A'. The chapter numbers in the ask are AFG's cell at OUR ROW INDEX, i.e. an index join (R20), and every one of them is a NEIGHBOURING episode's real chapter set that our catalog already anchors elsewhere: 156-157 is ep 89's, 184-188 is ep 122's, 58 is ep 130's graft, 194-196 is ep 128's, 200 is ep 133's, 221-224 is ep 155's. THE MECHANISM, provable on eighteen consecutive rows: AFG's Ranma table has its TITLE column in Japanese BROADCAST order and its CHAPTER/type column in the Digital-Remaster PRODUCTION order, so its own two columns are out of phase wherever the two orders differ; our rows follow AFL, which is a third order again (broadcast in most zones, production in others). Read AFG the way it was built — the chapter cell at index N belongs to PRODUCTION episode N — and AFG marks all seven targets *Filler, in perfect agreement with AFL. Row 14 is the only one where AFG's own title row carries chapters ('23, 24'), and that is the same misalignment displayed rather than joined: AFG cells 14-21 print 23-24 / 25-27 / 27-30 / *Filler / 30-32 / 33-34 / 35-36 / *Filler, which is exactly ranma.fandom's manga field for production episodes 14-21 (Abduction of P-Chan, Close Call, P-Chan Explodes, Pelvic [None], Enter Shampoo, Shampoo's Revenge, I Love You Ranma, I Am a Man [None]). Ch 23-24 are the opening two chapters of the Martial Arts Figure Skating Arc and they belong to OUR EP 15, where a manual anchor already sits. Independent confirmation on every row from two sources beyond AFL and AFG: ranma.fandom's episode infobox reads 'manga = None' for all seven (an explicit editorial value — the same field carries chapter links on the canon rows either side), and ja-Wikipedia marks all seven アニメオリジナル作品 in the live revision AND TVオリジナル in the 原作 column of oldid 88774966, a column whose neighbouring rows carry volume ranges that match our stored anchors exactly (17巻11=ch 179 ep 125; 19巻1-3=191-193 ep 126; 19巻4-8=194-198 eps 128/129; 19巻9=199 ep 132; 19巻10=200 ep 133; 21巻7-22巻1=219-224 eps 154/155) — a working control, so a TVオリジナル cell is a positive claim and not silence. Segment accounting under T28: every one of the seven has ZERO source segments — no significant share, not even a sliver — so no anchors (A1), no annotations and no type corrections. Ep 90's flashbacks are to the anime-original ep 58 (熱闘編40 暴れん坊娘リンリンランラン, itself TVオリジナル), so they are neither source nor weight. WHO LIED: animefillerguide, by publishing one table whose two columns are keyed to two different episode orders; and our pipeline, by joining that table on ROW INDEX instead of title (R20). AFL told the truth throughout.

anchor_hostile.why: A1 — CONFIRMED FILLER, no position. 'Pelvic Fortune-Telling? Ranma is the No. One Bride in Japan' (骨盤占い! らんまは日本一のお嫁さん, 1989-08-19) is built entirely on Kin Ono, Dr. Tofu's mother, who exists only in the anime; Dr. Tofu's mother never appears in the manga. SEGMENTS: none — zero source material, so there is no significant segment and no sliver to weigh; the remainder (the whole episode) is anime-original, T27 filler. EVIDENCE beyond AFL and AFG: (1) ranma.fandom's episode infobox reads manga = None, and the page states 'is the 17th episode of the 1989 Ranma ½ anime, though it was originally the 14th episode aired' — its aired number 14 is our row; (2) ja-WP's live 各話リスト carries the efn アニメオリジナル作品 on 第14話 骨盤占い, and the deleted 原作 column preserved at oldid 88774966 reads TVオリジナル on the same row while 第13話 and 第15-17話 carry 2巻9-3巻5 and 4巻5-10話 — the control holds. THE ONE REAL AFG CLAIM IN THIS WAVE, AND WHY IT IS WORTHLESS: AFG's row 14 does carry the title 'Pelvic Fortune-Telling' with chapters '23, 24' and no filler mark, but AFG's chapter column is keyed to the PRODUCTION order while its titles are in broadcast order. Its cells 14-21 read 23-24 / 25-27 / 27-30 / *Filler N/A / 30-32 / 33-34 / 35-36 / *Filler N/A, which is exactly ranma.fandom's manga field for production episodes 14-21: The Abduction of P-Chan (ch 23-24), Close Call! The Dance of Death On Ice (25-27), P-Chan Explodes! (27-30), Pelvic Fortune-Telling (manga = None), Enter Shampoo (30-32), Shampoo's Revenge (33-34), I Love You Ranma (35-36), I Am a Man (manga = None). AFG's own cell for THIS episode is therefore its row-17 '*Filler | N/A'. Ch 23-24 (愛しのシャルロット / リンクにくちづけ, the first two chapters of the Martial Arts Figure Skating Arc) are OUR EP 15's: both chapter pages name 'The Abduction of P-Chan' as their anime counterpart and our catalog already anchors ep 15 → 24 [23].

A1 — CONFIRMED FILLER, no position. 'Ling-Ling & Lung-Lung Strike Back!' (リンリン・ランランの逆襲, 1991-04-19). SEGMENTS: none. The episode's own wiki summary is 'Several characters refer/have flashbacks to events which took place in Ling-Ling & Lung-Lung's last appearance' — that earlier appearance is our ep 58 (熱闘編40 暴れん坊娘リンリンランラン), which ja-WP also marks TVオリジナル and AFL types Filler, so the flashbacks recap ANIME-ORIGINAL footage: not source material, and weightless besides. Ling-Ling and Lung-Lung are anime-only characters. EVIDENCE: (1) ranma.fandom infobox manga = None; (2) ja-WP efn アニメオリジナル作品 on 熱闘編第72話 and TVオリジナル in oldid 88774966's 原作 column, immediately after 第70-71話 = 15巻8-11話 (ch 154-157, our eps 88/89). THE PHANTOM: the ask's 'AFG canon ch 156-157' is not AFG's claim about this episode. AFG's own row carrying the title 'Ling-Ling & Lung-Lung Strike Back!' is row 88 and reads '*Filler | N/A'. '156, 157' is AFG's cell at INDEX 90, whose title there is 'When A Guy's Pride And Joy Is Gone (2)' — ranma.fandom gives that episode production number 90 and manga = Chapter 156 / 157, and it is OUR EP 89, already anchored 89 → 157 [156]. An index join (R20) moved ep 89's chapters onto ep 90.

A1 — CONFIRMED FILLER, no position. 'A Xmas Without Ranma' (乱馬がいないXmas, 1991-12-20) is an anime-original Christmas story: Akane shopping for a present, Soun and Genma discovering Christmas, the snowfall. SEGMENTS: none. EVIDENCE: (1) ranma.fandom infobox manga = None (production 125 / aired 123 — the aired number is our row); (2) ja-WP efn アニメオリジナル作品 on 熱闘編第105話 and TVオリジナル in oldid 88774966, sitting between 第103-104話 = 18巻 (our eps 121/122) and 第107話 = 17巻11話 (ch 179, our ep 125) — the control holds on both sides. A1 — CONFIRMED FILLER, no position. 'A Cold Day in Furinkan' (雪ん子冬物語, 1992-01-10) is an anime-original snow-child story — Ryoga finds a flute in a snowstorm, a record snowfall buries Furinkan, Genma under the kotatsu. SEGMENTS: none; the manga has no counterpart story. EVIDENCE: (1) ranma.fandom infobox manga = None (production 126 / aired 124); (2) ja-WP efn アニメオリジナル作品 on 熱闘編第106話 and TVオリジナル in oldid 88774966 (in the same rowspan block as 第105話), with 第107話 = 17巻11話 immediately after. THE PHANTOM, AND IT IS THE MOST MISLEADING OF THE SEVEN: AFG's own row carrying the title 'A Cold Day In Furinkan' is row 126 and reads '*Filler | N/A'. The ask's 'ch 58' is AFG's cell at INDEX 124, whose title there is 'The Missing Matriarch Of Martial Arts Tea!' — ranma.fandom gives that episode production number 124 and manga = Chapter 58, and it is OUR EP 130, the row Sean already ruled MIXED with graft{58} (T6/A44, 2026-08-27). So the number that looked like a new canon claim on ep 124 is the ep-130 ruling's own chapter, moved one file by the index join. Ch 58 is also the tail of the Martial Arts Tea Ceremony arc adapted at ep 93 (anchored 93 → 58 [56]); nothing of it is in ep 124.

structure.notes:
THE AFG TWO-ORDER DEFECT (the trap this wave paid for, and it is a SERIES-WIDE property of animefillerguide's Ranma page, not a Ranma property).

animefillerguide's Ranma ½ table publishes ONE table whose two columns are keyed to TWO DIFFERENT episode orders. Its TITLE column follows the Japanese broadcast order (第1期 1-18 then 熱闘編 1-143, so 'Enter Shampoo' is its row 15 and 'The Abduction of P-Chan' its row 25). Its CHAPTER-and-type column follows the Digital-Remaster PRODUCTION order that ranma.fandom prints as 'N (production order)' in every episode infobox. Where the two orders coincide the table looks correct; where they differ, the cell you read next to a title belongs to a different episode.

PROOF, eight consecutive rows at the head of the run (AFG cell -> ranma.fandom's manga field for the episode with that PRODUCTION number):
  AFG 14 '23, 24'            -> production 14 = The Abduction of P-Chan          = ch 23-24   (our ep 15)
  AFG 15 '25, 26, 27'        -> production 15 = Close Call! The Dance of Death    = ch 25-27   (our ep 16)
  AFG 16 '27, 28, 29, 30'    -> production 16 = P-Chan Explodes!                  = ch 27-30   (our ep 17)
  AFG 17 '*Filler | N/A'     -> production 17 = Pelvic Fortune-Telling            = manga None (our ep 14)
  AFG 18 '30, 31, 32'        -> production 18 = Enter Shampoo                     = ch 30-32   (our ep 18)
  AFG 19 '33, 34'            -> production 19 = Shampoo's Revenge                 = ch 33-34   (our ep 19)
  AFG 20 '35, 36'            -> production 20 = I Love You, Ranma!                = ch 35-36   (our ep 20)
  AFG 21 '*Filler | N/A'     -> production 21 = I Am a Man!                       = manga None (our ep 21)
and nine more at rows 22-30 (59-62 / 37-40 / 41-43 / 46-47 / 43-45 / 48-50 / 70-73 / 51-52 / 53-55 against productions 22-30 = Takeout Race, You Really Do Hate Cats, This Ol' Gal, Chestnuts, Enter Mousse, Cool Runnings, Danger at the Tendo Dojo, Ranma Trains on Mt. Terror, Breaking Point). Eighteen for eighteen.

WHY OUR ROWS SOMETIMES AGREE AND SOMETIMES DO NOT. Our row order is AFL's, which is a THIRD sequence: broadcast order in most of the run but the production/remaster order in the 14-30 and 88-90 and 121-135 and 154-156 zones (AFL rows 15-17 carry the figure-skating trio with December 1989 dates sitting between August/September rows — the tell). Title-keyed, AFG's row number differs from ours on 41 of 161 rows. So an INDEX join of AFG's chapter column onto our rows is right wherever AFL happens to agree with the production order and junk everywhere else. That is exactly the shape of the six phantom 'canon' claims in this wave, and it is the same defect that produced the six junk anchors Sean deleted under A6 on 2026-08-25 (eps 14, 90, 123, 131, 134, 156 — the identical row set, minus 124 which never carried one). R20 is the fix: join AFG on normalised TITLE, never on index.

HOW TO READ AFG ON RANMA CORRECTLY, IN ONE LINE: the chapter/type CELL at AFG index N describes the episode whose ranma.fandom 'production order' number is N; the TITLE printed beside it does not.

REFINEMENT OF THE STORED G54 RULING (not a contradiction — an added fact). G54 says 'Our row order is not the Japanese broadcast order — it follows the AFL/AFG sequence, which mixes production/aired order.' Confirmed, and now specified: ja-WP's 各話リスト (話数は実際に放送された順) and ranma.fandom's List-of-episodes page are BROADCAST order; ranma.fandom's per-episode infobox prints both numbers explicitly ('17 (production order) / 14 (aired order)'); AFG's titles are broadcast and its chapters production; our rows are AFL's mix. Every join on this series must be by title or air date.

THE FOURTH SOURCE THIS WAVE FOUND — ja-WP's DELETED 原作 COLUMN. ja-Wikipedia's らんま1/2 各話リスト used to carry a 原作 column giving each episode's volume-and-chapter-in-volume correspondence or the word TVオリジナル. It was removed some time between 2022-03 and 2023-05; the last revision that carries it is oldid 88774966 (2022-03-29, 30 TVオリジナル cells), and a Japanese fan blog (fumitom.blogspot.com, 2024-10) keeps a transcribed backup with the 通し話数 added. It is a per-episode chapter-level witness in VOLUME space and it agrees with ranma.fandom's chapter fields wherever both speak (17巻11話 = ch 179 = ep 125; 19巻1-3話 = 191-193 = ep 126; 19巻4-8話 = 194-198 = eps 128/129; 19巻9話 = 199 = ep 132; 19巻10話 = 200 = ep 133; 21巻7話-22巻1話 = 219-224 = eps 154/155; 6巻9-11話 = 56-58 on BOTH ep 93 and ep 130, matching the stored ep-93 anchor and the ep-130 graft). Its boundaries wobble by a chapter at a few arc seams (it gives 4巻5-10話 = ch 31-36 for eps 18-20 where the fandom's per-episode fields give 30-36), so it is a chapter-SET witness, not a page-split witness. Worth adding to the ranma toolkit and to any future 1980s-90s Shogakukan series with a ja-WP list.

REVERSE INDEX (corroborating only, and read as SILENCE not proof). None of the seven target episode pages has a single backlink from a Chapter page on ranma.fandom, while canon rows do (The Abduction of P-Chan <- Chapter 23, 24; When a Guy's Pride and Joy is Gone <- Chapter 156, 157; Bring It On! Love as a Cheerleader Part 2 <- Chapter 221-224). The index is incomplete — 'The Missing Matriarch of Martial Arts Tea!' and "Gosunkugi's Paper Dolls of Love" have no chapter backlinks either despite carrying ch 58 and ch 200 in their own infoboxes — so absence here is supporting texture, never the finding.

flags_for_sean: THE FLAG ITSELF IS THE DEFECT, not the data. Six of the seven rows in this wave (90, 123, 124, 131, 134, 156) were flagged as STRONG type_source_disagreement on the strength of an AFG chapter value that AFG never printed against that episode. The stored per-row AFG chapters/types for ranma-1-2 are index-joined (R20). Recommend: re-derive the AFG lane for this series joined on normalised TITLE, or suppress the AFG lane for ranma-1-2 entirely. Until then any future flag computed from AFG rows on this series is untrustworthy in BOTH directions — it will manufacture disagreements like these six and it will hide real ones.

AN AUDIT YOU CAN RUN WITHOUT A MODEL. For any series where AFG's title order and our row order differ, compare AFG's row number for each title against our row number; where they differ, the stored AFG chapter value on that row is the OTHER episode's. On ranma-1-2 that is 41 of 161 rows. This is mechanically checkable (P5/P30) and would have closed this wave's seven rows before a research agent was spent on them.

OUTSIDE THE ASK, QUEUED, NOT CORRECTED — ep 158 'A Ninja's Dog is Black and White' is stored MIXED (AFL: Mixed Canon/Filler) but three sources call it anime-original: ranma.fandom's infobox reads manga = None, ja-WP's live list marks it アニメオリジナル作品, and oldid 88774966's 原作 column puts it inside the rowspan TVオリジナル block covering 熱闘編 138-141 (our 156-159). AFG's row 158 (which is also production 158, so no misalignment here) reads *Filler | N/A. That is AFL alone against three. I have NOT typed it: a T28 verdict needs the episode's own content read for a sliver, which is outside this wave's rows. Same shape may apply to other AFL 'Mixed Canon/Filler' rows on this series (17, 22, 27, 34, 55) — worth a lane.

NO REPAIRS PROPOSED. All six previously-junk anchors (14, 90, 123, 131, 134, 156) are already deleted under Sean's A6 rulings of 2026-08-25 and the context confirms none is stored; ep 124 never carried one. The batch-17 A6 reason text described the mechanism as 'AFG's Ranma table is ordered by the Digital-Remaster/production sequence in several zones while our rows are in aired order' — right in direction, and now exactly specified in this verdict's structure notes (AFG's TITLES are broadcast, its CHAPTERS are production, our rows are AFL's mix). Worth folding that sentence into the ruling text so the next agent does not re-derive it.

The stored anchors that these phantom values were stolen from all check out against ranma.fandom's title-keyed episode fields: ep 15 {23-24}, ep 89 {156-157}, ep 122 {184-188} (the wiki's field reads 184-187; 188 comes from the arc table and the existing abridged{189-190} annotation), ep 128 {194-196}, ep 133 {200}, ep 155 {221-224}, and ep 130's graft{58}. Nothing in this wave asks to move any of them.
